content: The hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 plays a critical role in the metabolism of conjugated estrogens. 1. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Eluxadoline increases the levels of conjugated estrogens by reducing their metabolism. It may also increase systemic exposure to co-administered OATP1B1 substrates. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Encorafenib affects CYP3A4 metabolism by both inhibiting and inducing the enzyme at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may lead to increased toxicity or reduced efficacy. Caution and monitoring are required. 5. Ertapenem decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. It also increases estrogen levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and erythromycin lactobionate exhibit similar effects as erythromycin base, decreasing estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora and increasing levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. These interactions apply only to oral forms of the hormone. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 8. Erythromycin stearate decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora and increases levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. These effects are specific to oral forms of the hormone. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Eslcarbazepine acetate decreases estrogen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Etravirine reduces estrogen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 11. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of exenatide injectable solution and exenatide injectable suspension through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 12. Fedratinib increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments for CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Felodipine increases estrogen levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Fleroxacin decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 15. Fluconazole increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Fludrocortisone decreases estrogen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Fosamprenavir increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 18. Fosaprepitant increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Fosfomycin decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 20. Fosphenytoin decreases estrogen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Gemifloxacin decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 22. Gentamicin decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Grapefruit increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 24. Griseofulvin decreases estrogen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 25. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of hemin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may further decrease hemin efficacy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of hyaluronidase by enhancing tissue resistance to the enzyme. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Hydrocortisone decreases estrogen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 28. Indinavir increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of insulin degludec, insulin aspart, and inhaled insulin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance, necessitating glycemic monitoring in diabetic patients. 30. Conjugated estrogens decrease the levels of isavuconazonium sulfate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 31. Istradefylline increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. At 40 mg/day, it increases peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates, but this effect is not observed at 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 32. Ivosidenib decreases estrogen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Ketoconazole increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Conjugated estrogens decrease lamotrigine levels by increasing hepatic clearance. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 35. Lapatinib increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Lenacapavir increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. As a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, it may increase the levels of CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 37. Levofloxacin decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 38. Levoketoconazole increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Linezolid decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 40. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of liraglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 41. Conjugated estrogens decrease the levels of lonapegsomatropin by reducing serum insulin-like growth factor-1 response. Patients on oral estrogen replacement may require higher lonapegsomatropin dosages. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Lopinavir increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 43. Loratadine increases estrogen levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 44. Lovastatin increases estrogen levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Lumefantrine decreases estrogen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 46. Conjugated estrogens increase maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 47. Marijuana increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 48. Meropenem decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Meropenem/vaborbactam exhibits similar effects as meropenem, decreasing estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 50. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 51. Methylprednisolone decreases estrogen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 52. Metronidazole decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. It also increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 53. Miconazole vaginal increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 54. Mifepristone increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 55. Minocycline decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 56. Moxifloxacin decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 57. Nefazodone increases estrogen levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 58. Nelfinavir increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 59. Neomycin PO decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 60. Nevirapine decreases estrogen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 61. Nicardipine increases estrogen levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 62. Nifedipine increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and decreases levels by inducing P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 63. Nilotinib increases estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 64. Nitrofurantoin decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 65. Ofloxacin decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 66. Oxcarbazepine decreases estrogen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 67. Oxytetracycline decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 68. Paromomycin decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of the hormone. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 69. Pentobarbital decreases estrogen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 70. Phenobarbital decreases estrogen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are necessary.
